question: Unlocking final investment decisions along the carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) value chain

Article 23 of the Net-Zero Industry Act1 sets a binding target of 50 Mt CO₂ injection capacity per year by 2030. The Commission has identified CCUS as essential to meeting this target. Achieving this requires final investment decisions (FIDs) across the CCUS value chain in the near term.

However, FIDs remain stalled: capture projects depend on transport and storage availability, while storage developers need firm offtake commitments. Without coordinated action, the 50 Mt target will not be met. This is a coordination challenge the market cannot resolve alone.

The upcoming proposals concerning CO₂ markets and infrastructure (Q3 2026)2 and the Industrial Decarbonisation Bank (Q2 2026)3 are expected to address this, but concrete mechanisms are still unclear. 1.
What regulatory measures will the Commission propose in the CO₂ Markets and Infrastructure proposal to ensure FIDs in the CCUS value chain, and what is the timeline?

How will the Commission address the risk that emitters bear continued costs for complying with the Emissions Trading System (ETS) during value chain disruptions beyond their control, when capture is operationally unavailable4?

How will the Commission use the Industrial Decarbonisation Bank, alongside other financial de-risking instruments and regulatory measures (e.g. ETS-backed guarantees), to enable and accelerate early FIDs for CCUS projects?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 on establishing a framework of measures for strengthening Europe’s net-zero technology manufacturing ecosystem and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 (OJ L, 2024/1735, 28.6.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1735/oj).

2 Commission Work Programme 2026, ‘Development of CO₂ transportation infrastructure and markets,’ planned for Q3 2026. 3 Clean Industrial Deal (February 2025); proposal for Industrial Decarbonisation Bank planned for Q2 2026, EUR 100 billion envelope. 4 Zero Emissions Platform, response to EU public consultation on CO₂ markets and infrastructure, January 2026. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) The Commission is currently preparing a legislative proposal for adoption at the end of 2026 on CO₂1 Markets and Infrastructure. The proposal will include rules for developing an internal market for CO2. In terms of liability, under the Emissions Trading System (ETS) liability for the CO2 under their control is assigned to each value chain actor.

For emitters that capture CO2, there is indeed a commercial risk in case CO2 transport and CO2 storage services are not available, that they need to take into account. This risk is expected to reduce with the development of a more diversified, competitive storage market.

With the Innovation Fund the Commission is financially de-risking 60 Industrial Carbon Management projects with more than EUR 6 billion in committed grants that cover both investment and operational expenditures for CO2 services. Support to carbon capture, utilisation, and storage (CCUS) projects is also discussed in context of the announced Industrial Decarbonisation Bank.
